business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Federal Jurisdiction, Canada (Canada Business Corporations Act)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid; federal corporate law is common-law modeled, while Quebec retains civil law for provincial matters; common law applies in the other provinces and territories for private law matters.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement between Canada and the European Union (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended; Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; ISC/UBO register requirements under CBCA sections governing individuals with significant control (ISC), administered by Corporations Canada; sanctions framework under Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21, and Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of government-issued photographic identity document (passport or national identity card) for every proposed director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or national identity authority of the UBO's country of nationality or residency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada accession in force since January 11, 2024) or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Consular Legalization via the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant Canadian mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of charter document, certificate of good standing, or similar registry extract for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporation registry or registrar of companies in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization using the same foreign-affairs and Canadian-mission process as above

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed, notarized declaration or consent acknowledging the CBCA obligation to maintain an Individual Significant Control (ISC) register and to permit government access to UBO data
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Canadian notary public or lawyer licensed in the province or territory where the registered office will be located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only if executed in Canada; if executed abroad, Hague Apostille or consular legalization may be required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all candidates identified as domestic or foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates under FINTRAC and PCMLTFA guidance. Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorised signatories, and proposed counterparties against: (i) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) Canadian sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (iii) OFAC SDN List where transactions clear in USD via correspondent banks; (iv) UK/HM Treasury sanctions and consolidated financial sanctions targets list where international reinsurance counterparties require it; and (v) publicly available adverse media, law-enforcement, and regulatory enforcement databases. Adverse hits must be escalated immediately, and incorporation must be deferred until a negative screening result is confirmed and documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (ISED) / NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) portal; after clearance, filing is completed through Corporations Canada's online incorporation system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in English, French, or both official languages; a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporée, Limitée, or Corporation must appear in the name. Names must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing federal or provincial entity names or registered trademarks. Any non-Latin script name (Arabic, CJK, Cyrillic, etc.) must be transliterated into Latin script for the NUANS search and the approved transliteration becomes the statutory registry name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reserved name may be extended by filing a name reservation renewal request in Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre before expiry of the initial 90-day window. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to Corporations Canada within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching a revised or supplementary NUANS report, a legal brief on distinctiveness and non-confusion, and any required consents from the relevant regulator (for example, insurance name approval). If reconsideration is unsuccessful, judicial review may be sought in the Federal Court of Canada under the CBCA name provisions. A prudent applicant should simultaneously reserve a fallback name because the initial reservation is not automatically extended by the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible, with conditions. The CBCA requires a physical registered office in Canada at an address capable of receiving service of process and holding corporate records; a post office box alone is not acceptable. A law firm's or licensed corporate registered agent's physical address can serve as a virtual registered office if the agent accepts service and maintains the statutory records. For low-risk marine cargo surveying services where the company has no physical Canadian premises, this structure is generally accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Baseline risk of an unannounced federal CBCA compliance inspection for a non-distributing corporation is approximately 5% per annum. Activity-based inspections by provincial insurance, marine safety, or claims adjusting regulators occur mainly upon complaint or regulatory referral; for this low-risk ISIC 5222 marine insurance surveying scope the annual operational probability is estimated between 5% and 10%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and pre-clearance report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporations Canada / accredited NUANS service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or externally administered search tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 (CBCA), ss. 5–8 (incorporation), s. 19 (registered office), ss. 101 and 106 (directors), s. 121 (officers); Corporations Canada electronic filing policy
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) submitted through the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; the Articles fix the authorized share structure, commonly shares without par value, and consideration is determined by the directors. Escrow requirements do not arise at formation, but under CBCA s. 25 shares issued for property in a non-arm's length transaction may be subjected to escrow control as directed by the Director; regulated marine insurance service entities must also satisfy any capital and liquidity directives issued by the applicable provincial insurance regulator.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription agreements delivered by the subscribers as set forth in the register of share subscriptions be accepted, and the subscribed shares be issued and allotted against payment of the agreed consideration therefor; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors be confirmed and filed with Corporations Canada; RESOLVED, that the persons named in the Notice of Directors be and hereby are elected and appointed as the initial directors of the Corporation, to hold office until their successors are duly elected; RESOLVED, that the Board appoint the President, Secretary-Treasurer and such other officers as it deems necessary, with full authority to open bank accounts and effect regulatory filings; RESOLVED, that the by-laws, corporate seal and record-keeping procedures be adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Corporate Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED — NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) web portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name, including a legal element such as 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Limited', through the NUANS pre-registration portal. The search produces a report valid for 90 days listing confusingly similar corporate names and trademarks. Retain the NUANS report and reference number for attachment to the Articles of Incorporation. If the exact name is unavailable, instruct the portal to reserve the first available alternate name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and a minimum of two alternate names, including bilingual variants where applicable
NUANS online request confirmation and payment receipt (approximately CAD 13.80 per search)
Incorporator authorization letter or client engagement record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags confusing similarity with an existing trademark or corporate name, select an alternate name from the reserved list and obtain a fresh report; if the conflict is a trademark objection, the incorporator may obtain a consent letter from the trade-mark owner or adopt a distinct coined name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (electronic) or Companies Directorate, ISED, Ottawa (paper filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), including the NUANS report reference, share classes, dividend and voting rights, transfer restrictions if any, registered office street address (no post office box), first directors with complete contact details, and incorporator particulars. Confirm director residency: at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians, or, if fewer than four directors are appointed, at least one director must be a resident Canadian; the marine insurance survey corporation must appoint at least one director resident in Canada. Submit electronically and pay the CAD 200 online incorporation fee by credit card.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report dated within 90 days
Director nomination records and signed declarations of consent
Payment of the state filing fee (CAD 200 online / CAD 250 paper)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice issues, the applicant must cure the defect by submitting clarifications or amended Articles within the statutory re-filing period; if the application is deemed abandoned, a fresh application with a new fee must be filed. Material errors in issued Articles may later be corrected under CBCA s. 261.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada — incorporation file processing unit (forms filed as part of the same submission batch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors) concurrent with or immediately after the Articles of Incorporation. Provide the full civic street address of the registered office within the named province and the first directors' full legal names, residential addresses, consent declarations, and residency particulars necessary to satisfy the resident Canadian quota. The filed notice establishes the statutory record of the corporation's registered office and director slate.
required_dossiers: Form 2 — Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
Director consent declarations, including Form 6 where required by provincial law
Street address occupancy evidence, such as lease, title, or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada queries a post office box address or an incomplete residential address, replace the record by filing Form 3 (Change of Registered Office) or Form 4 (Change of Directors) and resubmit the corrected notice; an address defect is curable without abandoning the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Commencement of Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada — Office of the Director, Corporate Registry (issuance and certificate authentication)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon electronic approval, the Director issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the date of incorporation. The corporation comes into existence on that certificate date and obtains its legal name, organization number, and perpetual existence. Retrieve the certified copy of the Articles and the incorporation number, then open the statutory minute book using the incorporation bundle prepared by counsel.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
NUANS report and incorporation correspondence retained in the permanent corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, apply to the Director for a corrected certificate under CBCA s. 261; if the certificate is lost or misfiled, request an authenticated re-issue from the Corporate Registry (applicable re-issue fees apply).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Resolutions, Banking Authority, CRA Registration and Extra-Provincial Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online portal; provincial extra-provincial registries (e.g., Ontario Extra-Provincial Registry; Quebec Regie des entreprises) for registration of extra-provincial corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational board meeting: adopt by-law No. 1, approve the corporate seal, authorize share subscription receipts, appoint officers, and approve the banking resolution with specimen signatures. Register with CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain the 9-digit Business Number and program accounts (GST/HST, payroll RP, corporate income tax RC). Depending on physical provincial presence, register the federal corporation as an extra-provincial corporation in each province where it carries on business, including Ontario under the Corporations Information Act and Quebec as a registrant enterprise under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Align the Business Number, municipal business licence, and the marine surveying office location in a single regulatory compliance file.
required_dossiers: Federal Certificate of Incorporation and certified Articles
Organizational board minutes and by-law No. 1
Share subscription agreements and initial share register
Bank account opening resolution and specimen signature cards
CRA Business Number registration particulars and program account elections
Provincial extra-provincial registration forms and municipal business licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA program account activation is delayed, submit a correction through the Business Number amendment facility and request ministerial relief under section 227 of the Income Tax Act where failure occurred despite due diligence; if a provincial registry queries the extra-provincial application, cure by filing the omitted annual return or address update and paying any late-filing penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Provincial insurance and financial services regulators — e.g., Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA); Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), Quebec; Financial and Consumer Services Commission (FCNB), New Brunswick; municipal licensing authorities for the physical office premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Independent Adjuster Licence (marine hull and cargo line) under the applicable provincial Insurance Act, together with a municipal Business Operating Permit for the survey office; where the marine surveyor issues inspection reports only and does not negotiate settlements, the marine claim inspection exemption must be documented and relied upon in accordance with provincial insurance regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) for federal environmental duties; provincial ministries of environment (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks) for site-specific approvals
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA — office-based marine surveying activities are not a 'designated physical activity' under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 Schedule; a registration-level self-assessment for waste stream handling satisfies the federal and provincial threshold
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC-bearing process emissions are generated by claims inspection services; municipal sewer-use by-laws cap office sanitary discharge; packaging and e-waste must be recycled through certified facilities; any oil-contaminated samples taken during vessel or cargo surveys are transported under the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations and disposed of at approved hazardous waste depots

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and building occupancy certificate from the local fire marshal; structural load inspection for the registered office and any survey equipment storage; occupational health and safety registration under the Canada Labour Code (federal) or applicable provincial occupational health and safety statutes; for vessel boarding activities, clearance under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and Transport Canada navigation safety guidelines

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for GST/HST and federal corporate income tax administration; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs export control. Official portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/registration/business-registration-online.html).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owner marine survey corporation: (1) incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or register extra-provincially to obtain a corporate registry file number; (2) apply for the CRA 9-digit Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number'; (3) establish the RC (corporate income tax) program account and, where GST/HST registration is required or elected, the RT program account; (4) appoint a Canadian representative for service of process and submit the CRA non-resident ownership and Canadian address information; (5) no CBSA exporter identifier is required unless the surveyor itself arranges physical export of salvage or cargo.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Business Corporation is a taxable Canadian corporation under ITA s. 89(1) taxed at the entity level. Resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident corporations are taxed on Canadian-source business income only (territorial scope). No tax-exempt-zone benefits apply; zero-rated exports affect GST/HST cash flow only and do not alter income tax status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; entity classification follows corporate law and the CRA's administrative positions for foreign hybrids (e.g., U.S. LLCs). Available elections include: (i) the ITA s. 216 election to file a net-income return for Canadian real property rental income; (ii) the s. 219 branch-tax regime applicable to non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment; (iii) the GST/HST Quick Method election for eligible small registrants; (iv) the ETA s. 156 closely-related-corporations election for nil-consideration internal supplies; and (v) the selected-listed-financial-institution special attribution method (SAM) election. Hybrid-mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2, 18.3, 15(6.1)) restrict deduction/non-inclusion structures involving hybrid instruments or disregarded entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15; administered by the CRA, with Quebec GST and QST jointly administered by Revenu Québec where a Quebec permanent establishment exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: the CRA small-supplier threshold. A non-resident marine surveyor carrying on a business in Canada must register for GST/HST when its worldwide taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in four consecutive calendar quarters; voluntary registration is available to claim input tax credits, and registration can be mandatory without regard to the threshold where the non-resident is deemed to make taxable supplies in Canada under ETA s. 143.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based invoice pre-authorization, or digital stamping. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 300,000 must file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE for reporting periods ending on or after 1 January 2024, and must remit net tax electronically when the amount exceeds CAD 10,000. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoice Interoperability Framework is voluntary and Peppol-based; no CRA-operated invoice validator or government clearance code is required for zero-rated marine survey invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of the marine hull/cargo damage inspection supply is available under ETA Schedule VI, Part V: (a) section 1 zero-rates the supply of tangible personal property exported by the supplier; (b) section 5 zero-rates a service performed in respect of tangible personal property that is exported by or on behalf of the supplier; (c) sections 7 and 9 zero-rate a supply of services to a non-resident recipient where the service is not in respect of Canadian real property and not in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. For a survey-only engagement, the electronic delivery of the report to a non-resident underwriter is zero-rated where the inspected vessel or cargo is outside Canada at the time of inspection or is directly exported by or on behalf of the surveyor; otherwise the supply is deemed made in Canada and the 0% rate is unavailable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Export Declaration (B13A or Canadian Export Reporting System electronic confirmation) where the inspected cargo or vessel is physically exported
Bill of Lading evidencing the export movement of the surveyed goods or vessel
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-issued proof of FX receipt from the non-resident underwriter)
Executed marine survey engagement contract naming the non-resident recipient and specifying the 0% GST/HST rated supply
Final marine survey report with surveyor credentials, inspection location, and date-stamped evidence
Commercial invoice bearing the CRA GST/HST registration number and the non-resident billing address
Documentary proof of export (cargo manifest, customs transit document, or vessel clearance certificate) where the surveyed goods are exported after inspection
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess a zero-rated export claim within four years from the end of the reporting period, and without limitation where the return contains a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default. On audit, the exporter must produce the complete documentary export bundle on demand; failure to sustain the 0% rate triggers reassessment at the applicable GST/HST rate with daily compound interest, a default penalty under ETA s. 280 of 5% of the unreported net tax plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months), and a civil penalty under ETA s. 285 of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the net tax sought to be avoided for knowingly or grossly negligent false statements. Wilful evasion under ETA s. 327 is an indictable offence punishable by a fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Directors and officers may be jointly and severally liable under ETA s. 323 for unremitted amounts, penalties, and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada (central monetary authority); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (prudential regulator); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (AML/ATF intelligence). No dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration exists; exchange-rate policy is market-based under the Currency Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-52.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account; there is no administered rate and no prior authorization requirement for cross-border payments. Profit remittances are unrestricted at the exchange-control level, but dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced as low as 5% for a qualifying 10%+ corporate shareholder and typically 15% in default). Foreign-currency accounts such as USD operating and sweep accounts are ordinary products at Schedule I banks. The marine surveyor's USD fee income from offshore underwriters may be retained abroad or repatriated freely without any Bank of Canada filing or exchange-control license.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable in Canada. The Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, and no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation exists for export receipts or cross-border services invoices. USD survey fees received from foreign hull and cargo underwriters may be credited to a foreign-currency account and converted at commercial market rates whenever treasury policy requires CAD liquidity. The only binding cross-border reporting rule is FINTRAC obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, which require reporting of international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more and currency movement reports at the same threshold; these are informational AML/ATF filings, not exchange-control restrictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - CAD/USD with FX dealing platform
Operational Account - global trade and correspondent banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary disbursement rail; Low as sole treasury provider. Canada has no EU-style EMI or authorized payment institution licence, and the Bank Act reserves deposit-taking to chartered banks; an offshore digital EMI therefore cannot legally operate as the principal depository for CA_CORP. Wise Payments Canada Inc., registered as a money-services business with FINTRAC and as a payment service provider with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (in force November 2024), is viable for cross-border vendor payments and field-expense disbursements below 50,000 CAD per transaction, provided the Schedule I bank account remains the treasury anchor. Foreign unregistered EMIs must not solicit or receive funds from Canadian clients.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute mandates physical attendance. The Bank Act and PCMLTFA permit remote identification procedures, and Schedule I banks generally accept video KYC with notarized corporate documents for a low-risk standard-tier professional services entity. In practice, each bank's internal CDD policy may still require one in-person or recorded-video interview with at least one director; for an entirely non-resident directorate, banks typically demand an apostilled board resolution, certified passport copies, a Corporations Canada registry extract, a 25%+ ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of a Canadian registered office or local bookkeeper. Physical appearance is therefore a policy risk rather than a statutory mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with no physical Canadian business presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporations Canada registry extract; share register and beneficial-ownership schedule; FINTRAC-compliant UBO declaration form; foreign tax-residency certificates of all 25%+ shareholders; Canadian office lease or sublease; CRA corporate tax returns and Notice of Assessment; export service contracts with named marine insurers; and an organizational chart demonstrating substantive Canadian staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large USD wire receipts characterized as trade risk due to marine-insurance claim nomenclature
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory marine surveyor licence or recognized professional designation (Transport Canada or Class Society credential); valid professional-indemnity insurance certificate; signed survey orders from instructing underwriters (Lloyd's, P&I Clubs, hull syndicates); detailed survey invoices identifying NAICS 2022 code 488390; completed hull and cargo survey reports with policy numbers; and a letter from each instructing underwriter confirming the fee mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between a low-AML-risk professional service type and high cross-border transaction frequency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or internally reviewed financial statements for the last three fiscal years; cash-flow projection evidencing claim-cycle seasonality; client retainer and framework agreements; underlying claim attendance logs and expense receipts for disbursements; and a corporate AML/ATF policy appointing a compliance officer responsible for record keeping and suspicious-transaction reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on a third-party digital payment rail for international disbursement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution formally authorizing Wise or equivalent SPI rail usage with transaction ceilings; a cleared whitelist of approved beneficiary accounts; records demonstrating each disbursement traces to a documented marine survey expense; monthly reconciliation to the Schedule I operating account; and a vendor-order and expense-claim audit trail retained under the seven-year CRA record-keeping requirement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident parent injects equity via SWIFT MT103 to the RBC Capital Escrow Account in CAD; the remittance information field must cite OECD purpose code G101 (Direct investment - equity capital) or the bank-approved equivalent capital code, accompanied by board resolution, share subscription agreement, updated share register, and source-of-funds bank statement. No Bank of Canada approval or foreign-exchange license is required. The only federal filing triggered by the greenfield capital injection is the Investment Canada Act s.12 notification for the establishment of a new Canadian business, which the non-Canadian investor must duly file. The receiving bank verifies remitter identity, UBO registry data, and board authorization before crediting the escrow, after which funds move by internal transfer to the TD, BMO, or Scotiabank operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International fee settlements, reinsurance repayments, and third-party claim disbursements clear via SWIFT MT103 through the RBC or TD global correspondent network with SWIFT gpi end-to-end tracking. Canadian-dollar domestic obligations settle same-day through Payments Canada Lynx (RTGS) for high-value wires or through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for scheduled payroll, expense reimbursements, and CRA source-deduction remittances. Commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) are retained only where a reinsurer expressly requires lien-escrow collateralization of claim funds; all other service revenue settles on open-account wire terms. Wise Business handles ancillary field-disbursement and small vendor payments under the authorization governance described in the AML/KYC blueprint.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions (tenor up to 24 months) executed with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I dealer
Window and flexible CAD/USD forwards matched to uncertain marine claim settlement dates
Spot FX conversion upon receipt of underwriter fees, executed on the bank's electronic dealing platform
CAD/USD cross-currency interest-rate swaps executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with credit support annex for long-dated liabilities
FX swaps (short-dated rollovers) to fund payroll, CRA remittances, and professional-indemnity premium payments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to non-convertible emerging-market claim currencies such as IDR, VND, and EGP where survey fees are receivable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return - confirmation of registered office and directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing for two consecutive years triggers the Director's notice of dissolution under CBCA s.212(2); dissolution becomes final 90 days after notice unless the outstanding annual return is filed and the default is remedied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including financial statements, Schedule 9, Schedule 50, and provincial allocation schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end, e.g., December 31 year-end returns due June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month of default, capped at 12 months; repeat failures double the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month; CRA prescribed-rate interest is compounded daily; gross-negligence penalties may reach 50% of understated tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement of Remuneration and T4 Summary (employee source deductions, CPP, EI, and income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late information-return penalty under ITA s.162(5) with a minimum of CAD 100 and exposure up to CAD 7,500; unremitted source deductions attract additional penalties, prescribed-rate interest, and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5 Statement of Investment Income (dividends and interest paid to shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year of payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to the ITA s.162(5) sliding penalty; unreported distributions create T2 reassessment risk and shareholder disclosure mismatches.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and quarterly instalment remittances (GST/HST registration is mandatory once gross revenues exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; marine surveying fees are taxable at the applicable GST/HST rate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within three months after the end of the GST/HST reporting period, e.g., March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; quarterly instalments apply where net tax remitted exceeds CAD 3,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Excise Tax Act s.280 penalties: 5% of the net tax unpaid on late filing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; separate 6% failure-to-remit penalty; prescribed-rate interest accrues daily on amounts in arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register annual verification and updating of beneficial ownership records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada via registered office records; verified by directors in connection with the CBCA Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty; the register must be updated within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware of any change in significant control; an annual verification is performed at the meeting of shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CBCA s.21.4 creates a summary offence for failure to maintain or disclose the ISC register, punishable by a fine of up to CAD 5,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 6 months; directors and officers remain exposed for defaults.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial marine insurance surveyor or adjuster licence renewal, where provincial insurance-adjuster licensing law applies to claims surveying activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Applicable provincial financial services regulator, e.g., FSRA Ontario, AMF Quebec, or B.C. Financial Services Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the licence anniversary date or biennially in accordance with the governing provincial insurance statute
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlicensed adjusting or surveying activity may invalidate professional indemnity insurance coverage, trigger provincial regulatory enforcement proceedings, and undermine evidentiary admissibility of survey reports in marine claims litigation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CBCA default rule under s.163(1) requires shareholders to appoint an independent auditor at each annual meeting; there is no automatic revenue-based exemption. Non-distributing private corporations may waive the requirement by unanimous shareholder resolution under CBCA s.163(3); in practice, the accepted alternative is a CPA Canada review engagement. A full audit remains effectively mandatory for distributing corporations and is commercially required where lender, insurer, or reinsurer covenants demand audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations; IFRS as issued by the IASB for publicly accountable enterprises; both frameworks comply with CRA requirements for the T2 filing and the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA requires a current ISC register to be maintained at the registered office. Directors must record every agreement, share transfer, or corporate action creating or terminating significant control within 15 days of becoming aware of it. The CBCA Annual Return filed with Corporations Canada does not yet include UBO schedules, but Bill C-42 amendments to the CBCA (royal assent June 20, 2024) introduce a federal corporate beneficial ownership registry to be filed with ISED once the registry portal is operational; the ISC register should be maintained now to ensure full traceability for that future filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 300 - 1,000 per annum (approx. USD 220 - 740) for registered office and agent services, depending on scope of support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Full CBCA audit: CAD 6,000 - 15,000 (approx. USD 4,400 - 11,100); CPA review engagement: CAD 2,500 - 6,500 (approx. USD 1,850 - 4,800)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal-only rate; combined federal-provincial rate typically 25-31% depending on province of residence and allocation
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% (and provincial reductions to 8-14% combined) on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations; additional deductions for investment tax credits, scientific research and experimental development, and manufacturing/professional services tax measures

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed electronically via the CRA GST/HST Internet File Transfer or authorized E-services provider; paper filing mandatory only if internet filing not available
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly instalments required when federal/provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 due no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance of tax due no later than 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months for specified CCPCs with <CAD 500,000 taxable capital

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net business income from Schedule 1 (Income/Expenses) before loss carrybacks
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate surveyor must report Canadian-source business income attributable to a deemed permanent establishment; allocate income using GAAP methods

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions, loss carryovers, and elections
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty PE threshold; if no PE, Canadian business income may be exempt under numerous tax treaties; otherwise arrive at Part I taxable income under Code R

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% (28% for non-resident-owned investment corporations), reduced by SBD and investment tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to Part I on Canadian-source income; SBD normally unavailable unless the non-resident is a treaty resident with a PE in Canada and the corporation is not designated as a 'specified corporate form'

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial/territorial tax allocated by permanent establishment formula (Schedule 5)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provincial allocation requires an established PE in a province; treaty restrictions may eliminate provincial allocation if no domestic PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, rents, royalties, or management fees paid to the non-resident shareholder (if applicable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold and remit Part XIII at 25% (or reduced DTA rate) on amounts paid or credited to non-resident connected shareholders; file T106 and NR4

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months (maximum 17%), plus daily interest on late payments; instalment failure penalties for large corporations; failure to report a taxable transaction: $100 to $500 per form; continued failure to file a return for more than 10 years: increased penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For treaty-resident corporate shareholders, the beneficial owner must submit a Completed NR301 or NR302 form (Claim for Tax Treaty Relief) and a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction; the payee applies for relief before payment or applies for refund within 2-3 years; reduced rate generally 5% if the corporate shareholder owns ≥10% of voting shares, otherwise 15%; US/Canada treaty aligns.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory; treaty rates typically 10% (industrial/commercial royalties) and 0% for certain computer software and patent royalties under Canada-US treaty; Interest: 25% statutory; 0% for arm's length non-residents under Canadian domestic exemption, treaty rates generally 10% for related-party interest, 15% or 0% under US treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate controlled transactions (goods, services, intangibles, interest or fees) with all non-resident related persons triggers mandatory T106 filing; Canada does not prescribe formal Local File/Master File documents, but contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be provided when requested by CRA; Country-by-Country Reports required for consolidated groups with ≥ EUR 750 million revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no general Economic Substance Regulations, but the GAAR (s. 245) may void an avoidance transaction that lacks substantive commercial purpose; the 'permanent establishment' test and the 'treaty shopping' limitations require actual business activity, board oversight, and risk-taking in Canada for a marine surveyor corporation; insurance brokers and surveyors licensed in Canada must maintain a physical office and professional staff.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully evading or attempting to evade tax liability by failing to file T2 return, suppressing marine survey income, falsifying log books or expense records, or claiming fictitious PE losses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil gross-negligence penalty 50% of understated tax plus daily interest; CRA may seize assets through Tax Court judgment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for corporation's unremitted source withholdings, GST/HST, and 50% of unpaid penalty amounts if they failed to exercise required diligence (s. 227.1 and s. 323); court-ordered civil restitution, asset freeze, travel-hold through departure prohibition orders, and potential imprisonment for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Materially understating Canadian taxable income by charging below arm's-length fees for marine insurance survey services or inflating royalties/reimbursements paid to non-resident affiliate without contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at arm's length price; penalty of 10% of adjusted net amount if documentation absent; CRA may impose 10% 'transfers of pricing violation' penalty and refuse treaty relief; criminal prosecution for fraudulent misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or participated in misrepresentation are personally liable for the penalty and additional federal tax (s. 227.1); exclusion from cross-border board appointments; travel restrictions under the Income Tax Act departure prohibition

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Canadian corporation with no real office, employees, bank account, or substantive marine survey activity for the purpose of claiming tax treaty benefits under the Canada-US DTA or avoiding the Canada Revenue Agency's PE audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of GAAR s. 245 to re-determine the tax consequences, denial/termination of treaty benefits, amended assessments with interest and penalties up to 50% of understated tax; corporate name strike-off and revocation of T2 registration; possible criminal sanction if the shell is used for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be sued for restitution of distributions received from the shell; May be subject to 'piercing the corporate veil' if the corporation was interposed for a dominant fraudulent or misrepresentation purpose; Court may issue costs orders and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as a marine insurance surveyor under provincial licensing regimes (e.g., Ontario's Insurance Act, 2020's Adaptations), accepting cash payments above CAD 10,000 without reporting, or failing to keep transaction records for CRA's crypto-asset reporting and AML regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines up to CAD 250,000 for individuals and CAD 1 million for corporate entities; licence suspension or cancellation; CRA may impose Remittance-Withholding Penalties and suspend the T2 return processing; FINTRAC monetary penalties up to CAD 1.5 million for each violation; prohibition from participating in government procurement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for fines under provincial insurance statutes if they knowingly permit non-registered practice; in serious cases, personal imprisonment under AML laws up to 3 years; travel bans under the Federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act
